Minor water-bearing units in the SJMA show transmissivity values of 200–500 ft²/d. • Middle Confining Unit: Consists of low-permeability rocks, including the upper Cibao Formation, Quebrada Arenas Limestone, Río Indio Limestone, and mudstone. It generally restricts vertical flow, but test holes (NC-15 at 1,268 ft and NC-1 at 635 ft) 10 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. suggest it may be leaky, allowing water from the lower aquifer to move upward into the upper aquifer in the SJMA. • Lower Aquifer: Composed of the Lares Limestone, the Montebello Limestone Member of the Cibao Formation, and shallow facies of the Mucarabones and San Sebastián formations. It is thickest and most transmissive in the north-central part of the basin; its extent west of Río Grande de Arecibo is uncertain. The Montebello Limestone Member shows transmissivity values ranging from 625 to 3,600 ft²/d, with the highest values between Río Grande de Arecibo and Río Grande de Manatí (~30 km west of San Juan). Additionally, the Mucarabones Sand aquifer within the SJMA has estimated transmissivity values of 850–1,000 ft²/d, making it a significant but underutilized water- bearing unit (Gómez-Gómez 1987; Rodríguez-Martínez 1995).
